	<item>
		<title>Hilary Pecis Paints Saturated Snapshots of West Coast Life</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/hilary-pecis-love-letters-paintings/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 08 May 2026 22:02:22 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pecis-4.jpg" alt="Hilary Pecis Paints Saturated Snapshots of West Coast Life" />In Love Letters, Hilary Pecis captures the mundane moments and under-appreciated views of daily life. </p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? 										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pecis-4.jpg" alt="Hilary Pecis Paints Saturated Snapshots of West Coast Life" />


<p>In <em>Love Letters</em>, <a href="https://www.hilarypecis.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Hilary Pecis</a> captures the mundane moments and under-appreciated views of daily life. The Los Angeles-based artist presents a suite of new acrylic paintings in her signature saturated style, focusing on snippets of a backyard pool, the corner of a studio worktop, and a friendly picnic complete with a radiant strawberry cake. </p>



<p>Pecis prefers to work from photos and translates singular moments onto linen. Utilizing a uniform opacity in her paints, she incorporates both comparable and exaggerated colors and affords particular attention to texture and pattern. Frilly fronds on a plant, light radiating off the water&#8217;s surface, and the rough texture of a woven tablecloth each evidence the artist&#8217;s meticulous process.</p>



<p><em>Love Letters</em> opens at <a href="https://www.davidkordanskygallery.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">David Kordansky Gallery</a> in Los Angeles on May 16 and runs through June 20. Until then, explore more of Pecis&#8217; work on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/hilary_pecis/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img fetchpriority="high" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2398" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5.jpg" alt="a vibrant painting by Hilary Pecis of a backyard in ground pool with a donut shaped floaty" class="wp-image-473859" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5-640x767.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5-960x1151.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5-768x921.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5-1281x1536.jpg 1281w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ecis-5-1708x2048.jpg 1708w" sizes="(max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Pool&#8221; (2026), acrylic on linen, 92 x 77 x 1 5/8 inches</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Collaged Denim Sculptures by Nick Doyle Unravel American Mythology</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/nick-doyle-denim-sculptures/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Fri, 08 May 2026 18:11:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[denim]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Nick Doyle]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[United States]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473840</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-7.jpg" alt="Collaged Denim Sculptures by Nick Doyle Unravel American Mythology" />"The world's image of America has changed, but our country's nostalgia for itself is making us late to the party."</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/nick-doyle-denim-sculptures/">Collaged Denim Sculptures by Nick Doyle Unravel American Mythology</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-7.jpg" alt="Collaged Denim Sculptures by Nick Doyle Unravel American Mythology" />


<p>Despite its name, the Canadian Tuxedo is a distinctly American look. The denim-on-denim getup dates back to the 1950s, when Bing Crosby sported <a href="https://www.cbc.ca/radio/q/blog/did-bing-crosby-invent-the-canadian-tuxedo-1.4181725" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">a full Levi&#8217;s ensemble</a> while in Vancouver, setting a sartorial trend that continues today.</p>



<p>The national mythology woven into this utilitarian material is also the focus of Brooklyn-based <a href="https://www.perrotin.com/en/artists/nick-doyle" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Nick Doyle</a>, who layers denim atop denim into large wall sculptures. From a pair of aviators reflecting puffy clouds to a vast Rocky Mountain landscape framed by brick, the works evoke a sort of nostalgic road trip west, as if chasing a big break, and ultimately, realizing the American dream.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="824" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2.jpg" alt="a large denim wall sculpture by Nick Doyle of sunglasses with clouds in the lenses" class="wp-image-473849" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2-640x264.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2-960x396.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2-768x316.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-2-1536x633.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;First Come the Dreamers&#8221; (2026), bleached and collaged denim on panel, 25 x 72 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>For Doyle, denim is a poignant, loaded metaphor for much of American culture and history. The material has roots in chattel slavery, when <a href="https://woub.org/2023/01/04/discover-the-fascinating-story-of-an-iconic-american-garment-riveted-the-history-of-jeans-on-american-experience-feb-7-at-9-pm/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">people enslaved in the South</a> were dyeing cotton with indigo. There&#8217;s also its association with the brusque masculinity of James Dean and cowboy ruggedness, itself an extension of the gold rush and Manifest Destiny. The fabric, in many ways, is a stand-in for the contradictions, hypocrisies, and unreachable desires so bound up in American life.</p>



<p>While researching the visual language of Americana in 2018, Doyle came upon a roll of denim discarded by a fashion designer moving out of his building. &#8220;At the time, I had no money, so I was making work out of material I&nbsp;found&nbsp;in the garbage or at my local hardware store,&#8221; he shares. &#8220;As I was pulling [the roll] out of the trash, I noticed a network of ideas connecting in my brain&#8230;&nbsp;I felt the material reflected the historical complexities I was seeing in my research, as well as being reflected in my own familial history.&#8221;</p>



<p>This encounter was one of those providential moments that set off an enduring fascination. In his solo exhibition <em>Collective Hallucinations</em>, on view at Perrotin, Doyle presents the latest of his denim sculptures, including stylized cacti, landscapes cordoned off by chainlink fences, and more mystical objects like tarot cards and a life-sized fortune teller&#8217;s shop. </p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2196" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5.jpg" alt="a large denim wall sculpture by Nick Doyle of a landscape shown throw a brick wall" class="wp-image-473851" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5-640x703.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5-960x1054.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5-768x843.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5-1399x1536.jpg 1399w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-5-1865x2048.jpg 1865w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Innocent Industry&#8221; (2026), bleached and collaged denim on panel, 72 x 64 inches</figcaption></figure>



<p>The show contains myriad symbols of American exceptionalism and individualism, presented in the heritage fabric of the nation. Doyle shares:</p>



<blockquote class="wp-block-quote is-layout-flow wp-block-quote-is-layout-flow">
<p>Over the last few years, my conception of American mythology has only become more complex&#8230; I think in a lot of ways what we&#8217;re experiencing now is a breakdown of these mythologies. They are in direct conflict with the current political reality, yet they are summoned as if it is business as usual. The world&#8217;s image of America has changed, but our country&#8217;s nostalgia for itself is making us late to the party. There&#8217;s tragedy in vanity.</p>
</blockquote>



<p><em>Collective Hallucinations</em> presents these unrealized dreams and confrontations in varying shades of blue, rendering what appears to be individual moments as simply different washes of the same story. </p>



<p>In addition to his practice, Doyle will soon open a kink bar called Human Resources and is working toward a fall exhibition of paper collages and prints at Pace. If you&#8217;re in New York, <em>Collective Hallucinations</em> runs through May 30. Otherwise, find more on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/nickdoyle333/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="3000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9.jpg" alt="a large denim wall sculpture by Nick Doyle of a cactus" class="wp-image-473855" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-9-1365x2048.jpg 1365w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Here We Go Round the Prickly Pear Bush&#8221; (2026), bleached and collaged denim on panel, 48 x 26 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2615" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6.jpg" alt="a large denim wall sculpture by Nick Doyle of a cloud tarot card" class="wp-image-473852" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6-640x837.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6-960x1255.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6-768x1004.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6-1175x1536.jpg 1175w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/doyle-6-1566x2048.jpg 1566w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;The Clouds&#8221; (2026), bleached denim on panel, 24 x 18 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1931" height="2896" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle.jpg" alt="a large denim wall sculpture by Nick Doyle of a cactus with a flamingo in the center" class="wp-image-473856" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle.jpg 1931w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle-640x960.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle-960x1440.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle-768x1152.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle-1024x1536.jpg 1024w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/2-Nick-Doyle-1366x2048.jpg 1366w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1931px) 100vw, 1931px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Plastic Eden&#8221; (2026), bleached and collaged denim on panel, 68 x 42 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1235" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle.jpg" alt="" class="wp-image-473857" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle-640x395.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle-960x593.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle-768x474.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/3-Nick-Doyle-1536x948.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Black Market Bodies&#8221; (2026), bleached and collaged denim on panel, 36 x 64 inches</figcaption></figure>

]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-5.jpeg" alt="In &#8216;Reverence,&#8217; Three Decades of Paul Nicklen&#8217;s Remarkable Photographs Exalt Nature" />


<p>Known for his stunning photos of <a href="/tags/paul-nicklen">wildlife and landscapes</a>, as well as co-founding <a href="https://sealegacy.org/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">SeaLegacy</a> alongside fellow conservationist and photographer <a href="/tags/cristina-mittermeier">Cristina Mittermeier</a>, <a href="https://paulnicklen.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Paul Nicklen</a> has traveled the globe to not only highlight our planet&#8217;s phenomenal biodiversity but also to shed light on its increasing vulnerabilities due to the ongoing climate crisis.</p>



<p>Nicklen&#8217;s most ambitious project yet gathers myriad images from a career exploring the corners of the earth for more than three decades. Forthcoming from Hemeria, <em><a href="https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-book-reverence" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Reverence</a></em> marks the most comprehensive collection of his work to date. The book features 160 photographs, including some of Nicklen&#8217;s most enduring images alongside others previously unpublished.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9.jpeg" alt="A close-up photograph by Paul Nicklen of a lion cub" class="wp-image-473807" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-9-1536x1024.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>From the root-like system of the Colorado River delta to narwhals feeding on cod in the Arctic Bay off Baffin Island, Nicklen&#8217;s photos illuminate the vast and resilient beauty of the natural world. &#8220;Reverence is what we feel in the silent presence of a whale beneath the ice, in the fierce gaze of a polar bear, in the timeless dance of ocean and light,&#8221; says a statement. &#8220;It is what the natural world evokes when we stop long enough to truly see it.&#8221;</p>



<p><em>Reverence </em>is slated for release on July 28, which is also World Conservation Day, and <a href="https://hemeria.com/en-us/products/the-book-reverence" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">pre-orders</a> are open now.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4.jpeg" alt="A close-up photograph by Paul Nicklen of a large colony of penguins" class="wp-image-473814" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-4-1536x1024.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1463" height="908" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-8.jpeg" alt="A spread from Paul Nicklen's book 'REVERENCE'" class="wp-image-473816" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-8.jpeg 1463w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-8-640x397.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-8-960x596.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/reverence-8-768x477.jpeg 768w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1463px) 100vw, 1463px" /></figure>

		<title>Explore 25 Incredible Photos of the Milky Way Captured Around the World</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/milky-way-photographer-of-the-year-contest-2026/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 07 May 2026 20:05:11 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Nature]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>

		<category><![CDATA[landscapes]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Milky Way Photographer of the Year]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[space]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473818</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-8.jpg" alt="Explore 25 Incredible Photos of the Milky Way Captured Around the World" />Organized by Capture the Atlas, the 2026 Milky Way Photographer of the Year saw a record number of submissions from around the globe.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/milky-way-photographer-of-the-year-contest-2026/">Explore 25 Incredible Photos of the Milky Way Captured Around the World</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-8.jpg" alt="Explore 25 Incredible Photos of the Milky Way Captured Around the World" />


<p>Organized by Capture the Atlas, the 2026 <a href="https://capturetheatlas.com/milky-way-photographer-of-the-year/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Milky Way Photographer of the Year</a> saw a record number of submissions, with more than 6,500 entries representing a wide range of landscapes and perspectives around the world. Just 25 were selected as the top images, representing 12 different regions from the Canary Islands to New Zealand to Argentina.</p>



<p>&#8220;Every year, this collection reminds us that photographing the Milky Way is not only about technique or planning. It is about curiosity, patience, and the desire to experience the night sky in places where it still feels wild,” says Dan Zafra, editor of Capture the Atlas and curator of the annual contest. “Many of these skies are becoming increasingly rare, and we hope these images inspire people not only to admire them, but also to value and protect them.”</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2161" height="1080" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3.jpg" alt="a stunning photo of the vibrant milky way in a star studded sky" class="wp-image-473823" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3.jpg 2161w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3-640x320.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3-960x480.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3-768x384.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3-1536x768.jpg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/milky-way-3-2048x1024.jpg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2161px) 100vw, 2161px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Brendan Larsen, &#8220;Milky Way over Syme Hut and Mt. Taranaki.&#8221; Syme Hut, Mt Taranaki, New Zealand​</figcaption></figure>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-7.jpg" alt="Jake Messing&#8217;s Hyperrealistic Paintings Celebrate the Abundance of Nature" />The Northern California-based artist explores nature as a reflection of our inner lives.</p>

										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-7.jpg" alt="Jake Messing&#8217;s Hyperrealistic Paintings Celebrate the Abundance of Nature" />


<p>&#8220;The world hums with beauty and danger, harmony and discord,&#8221; says <a href="https://www.jakemessing.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Jake Messing</a>. &#8220;We walk through these shifting currents every day. For as long as I can remember, I have turned toward the natural world—studying its patterns, its relationships, its quiet lessons.&#8221;</p>



<p>In highly detailed, hyperrealistic paintings, the Northern California-based artist explores nature as a reflection of our inner lives. Abundance and beauty are sometimes confronted with tension and discomfort, and through nature, &#8220;I question the fears and unspoken rules that shape us,&#8221; Messing says.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2663" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6.jpg" alt="A hyperrealistic, detailed still life painting of florals, succulents, and birds" class="wp-image-473785" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6-640x852.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6-960x1278.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6-768x1023.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6-1154x1536.jpg 1154w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-6-1538x2048.jpg 1538w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Coccinellidaes Hideaway 2&#8221;</figcaption></figure>



<p>Working in acrylic on canvas, the artist composes otherworldly vignettes of flora and fauna, often uniting creatures and plants in situations we&#8217;d be unlikely to encounter in the real world. Yet these dense, maximal clusters of succulents, insects, blossoms, birds, and other creatures summon what Messing describes as both &#8220;chaos and grace&#8221; in a vibrant meditation on ecosystems,  interdependency, and biodiversity.</p>



<p>In an art historical sense, these works certainly nod to the meticulously detailed <a href="/tags/dutch-golden-age-painting">Dutch Golden Age</a> oil paintings of the likes of <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2025/03/rachel-ruysch-nature-into-art/">Rachel Ruysch</a> and Jan Brueghel the Elder, which were also typically set against deep backgrounds. Employing a bit of <em>memento mori</em>—a reminder of the inevitability of death—these often incorporated wilting petals and other nods to decay.</p>



<p>Messing taps into this tradition, yet he emphasizes full-blooded vivacity. Every floret and frond is bursting with life, while the occasional playful color gradient, bubbles, or shiny fabric place these compositions firmly in our time. &#8220;Through my work, I seek to bring the outside in, to honor the wildness that surrounds us, and to reveal the beauty and danger, the decay and renewal, that bind our outer and inner worlds together,&#8221; he says.</p>



<p>See more on the artist&#8217;s <a href="https://www.instagram.com/jakemessing/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2962" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5.jpg" alt="A hyperrealistic, detailed still life painting of florals and bubbles" class="wp-image-473784" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5-640x948.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5-960x1422.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5-768x1137.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5-1037x1536.jpg 1037w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/messing-5-1383x2048.jpg 1383w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Bubbles and Blooms&#8221;</figcaption></figure>

		<title>Irina Werning Chronicles 18 Years of Photographing &#8216;Las Pelilargas&#8217; in a New Book</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/irina-werning-las-pelilargas-photography-portraits-book/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Thu, 07 May 2026 13:25:36 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Books]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[hair]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Indigenous culture]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Irina Werning]]></category>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-1.jpg" alt="Irina Werning Chronicles 18 Years of Photographing &#8216;Las Pelilargas&#8217; in a New Book" />Werning's chronicle of a time-honored Latin American Indigenous tradition highlights patience, joy, and cultural pride.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/irina-werning-las-pelilargas-photography-portraits-book/">Irina Werning Chronicles 18 Years of Photographing &#8216;Las Pelilargas&#8217; in a New Book</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-1.jpg" alt="Irina Werning Chronicles 18 Years of Photographing &#8216;Las Pelilargas&#8217; in a New Book" />


<p>For the better part of two decades, <a href="https://irinawerning.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Irina Werning</a> has traveled throughout Latin America searching for a specific trait: incredibly long hair. In her photography series <em><a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2024/03/irina-werning-las-pelilargas/">Las Pelilargas</a></em>—meaning &#8220;the long-haired ones&#8221; in Spanish—she chronicles a time-honored Indigenous tradition through a visual celebration of patience, joy, and cultural pride.</p>



<p>In a statement, Werning shares that when she asks young women in the many small towns she&#8217;s visited why they have long hair, they respond with simple reasons akin to, &#8220;Because I like it.&#8221; But, Werning adds, &#8220;The true reason is invisible and passes from generation to generation. It&#8217;s the culture of Latin America, where our ancestors believed that cutting hair was cutting life, that hair is the physical manifestation of our thoughts and our souls and our connection to the land.&#8221;</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1362" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7.jpg" alt="A line of young women with very long hair, facing away from the camera" class="wp-image-473763" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7-640x436.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7-960x654.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7-768x523.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-7-1536x1046.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>Nearly 90 images are included in Werning&#8217;s new book, <em>Las Pelilargas</em>, published by GOST Books. The photos span 18 years, starting with the artist&#8217;s first encounter with long-haired women in 2006 in Argentina, when she was photographing members of the Indigenous <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Qulla" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Kolla</a> community. </p>



<p>&#8220;Guided by her intuition, she went on to spend months in remote mountain towns putting up signs in schools, hospitals, and markets, and organising hair competitions in an effort to seek out those with long hair,&#8221; GOST says. Werning continued to make the portraits until 2024. &#8220;She found that traditions were not just surviving, but evolving with long hair symbolising both continuity and subtle rebellion.&#8221;</p>



<p>Find your copy on <a href="https://bookshop.org/a/96/9781805980162" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Bookshop</a>. You might also enjoy Celia D. Luna&#8217;s series, <em><a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2023/01/celia-luna-cholitas/">Cholitas Bravas</a>.</em></p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1334" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4.jpg" alt="A group of young women with very long hair stand and throw their locks very high into the air" class="wp-image-473760" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-4-1536x1025.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2915" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2.jpg" alt="A trio of young women on a bunk bed with very long black hair draped over the edge of the bed" class="wp-image-473758" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2-640x933.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2-960x1399.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2-768x1119.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2-1054x1536.jpg 1054w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-2-1405x2048.jpg 1405w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1499" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6.jpg" alt="A group of young women with very long hair sit along a stone wall in a line" class="wp-image-473762" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-6-1536x1151.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1365" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3.jpg" alt="A black-and-white photo of three young women with long black hair, near a stone wall" class="wp-image-473759" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3-640x437.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3-960x655.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3-768x524.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/pelilargas-3-1536x1048.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Luscious Hair Sculptures Sprout Like Branches in a Symbiotic Exhibition</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/merryn-omotayo-alaka-sam-fresquez-hair-sculptures/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 06 May 2026 18:38:22 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[hair]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[installation]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Merryn Omotayo Alaka]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Sam Frésquez]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[sculpture]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473721</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-4.jpg" alt="Luscious Hair Sculptures Sprout Like Branches in a Symbiotic Exhibition" />Merryn Omotayo Alaka and Sam Frésquez's synthetic hair sculptures suspend from the ceiling and splay across the floor like organic growths.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/merryn-omotayo-alaka-sam-fresquez-hair-sculptures/">Luscious Hair Sculptures Sprout Like Branches in a Symbiotic Exhibition</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-4.jpg" alt="Luscious Hair Sculptures Sprout Like Branches in a Symbiotic Exhibition" />


<p>A visit to Lincoln Park or the Garfield Park Conservatory is one of the outings Chicagoans rarely pass up, particularly when we need some reprieve from all the concrete and steel. Two beloved green spaces in the city, these spots boast oases blanketed in verdant foliage even in the depths of winter and house an array of specimens not native to the Midwest. </p>



<p>For artists <a href="https://www.merrynalaka.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Merryn Omotayo Alaka</a> and <a href="https://www.samfresquez.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Sam Frésquez</a>, the immersive nature of a conservancy, with plants above and below and all around, became a central point for a collaborative project. <em>Your Birth is My Birth</em> presents the duo&#8217;s synthetic hair sculptures, which suspend from the ceiling of <a href="https://www.janelombardgallery.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Jane Lombard Gallery</a> and splay across the wooden floor like organic growths. Alaka and Frésquez describe the exhibition as a sort of &#8220;Kanekalon forest,&#8221; referring to the brand behind the luscious material.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1546" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1.jpg" alt="people walk through a collection of suspended hair sculptures at various lengths. one emerges from pods on the floor" class="wp-image-473723" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1-640x495.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1-960x742.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1-768x594.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-1-1536x1187.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;Your Birth is My Birth.&#8217; Photo by Adam Reich</figcaption></figure>



<p>Five different &#8220;species&#8221; emerge in the space, including <em>Listening Roots</em>, <em>Hearing Bells</em>, <em>Mother &amp; Child</em>, <em>Stacking Pearls</em>, and <em>Umbra Pods</em>. Dark, dyed locks and domed shapes are throughlines, although each takes on a distinctive form. The series are influenced by <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Epiphyte" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">epiphytes</a>, non-parasitic plants that make their homes on a host specimen. Think orchids, cacti, moss, and kelp.</p>



<p>Surging upward from lily pad-shaped discs suctioned to the floorboards, the largest sculpture is part of <em>Listening Roots</em>, which tethers singular shoots to a central form. This connection between smaller pieces—like the feather-duster-shaped <em>Stacking Pearls</em>—and more comprehensive structures recurs throughout the exhibition, gesturing toward an intimate and intentional symbiosis.</p>



<p>Several works also reference genetics and what&#8217;s passed down through generations, as mirrored forms emerge within the same vertical tendril. &#8220;Similar to an epiphyte and its host tree, these sculptural works have their own life cycles evoking systems of dependence and exchange, where one form sustains from another,&#8221; says a statement.</p>



<p><em>Your Birth is My Birth</em> is on view through June 13. Explore more from <a href="https://www.instagram.com/merrynalaka/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Alaka</a> and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/samfresquez/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Frésquez</a> on Instagram.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1876" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8.jpg" alt="a hair sculpture that swooshes out onto the floor with three bulbs at the top like a handle" class="wp-image-473730" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8-640x600.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8-960x900.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8-768x720.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-8-1536x1441.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">&#8220;Stacking Pearl (Adolescent) I&#8221; (2026), Kanekalon hair and steel support, 24 x 24 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1507" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2.jpg" alt="a collection of suspended hair sculptures at various lengths" class="wp-image-473724" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2-640x482.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2-960x723.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2-768x579.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-2-1536x1157.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;Your Birth is My Birth.&#8217; Photo by Adam Reich</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="2126" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6.jpg" alt="a detail the underside of a hair sculpture with a wide bell shape and smaller fringe inside" class="wp-image-473728" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6-640x680.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6-960x1020.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6-768x816.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6-1445x1536.jpg 1445w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-6-1927x2048.jpg 1927w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail of &#8220;Umbra Pods I&#8221; (2026), Kanekalon hair and steel support, 45 x 27 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1500" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3.jpg" alt="a collection of suspended hair sculptures at various lengths. one emerges from pods on the floor" class="wp-image-473725" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3-640x480.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3-960x720.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3-768x576.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-3-1536x1152.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;Your Birth is My Birth.&#8217; Photo by Adam Reich</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1827" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7.jpg" alt="a detail the underside of a hair sculpture with a wide bell shape and smaller fringe inside" class="wp-image-473729" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7-640x585.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7-960x877.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7-768x702.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-7-1536x1403.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Detail of &#8220;Umbra Pods III&#8221; (2026), Kanekalon hair and steel support, 45 x 27 inches</figcaption></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1404" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5.jpg" alt="a collection of suspended hair sculptures at various lengths and some emerge from pods on the floor" class="wp-image-473727" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5-640x449.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5-960x674.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5-768x539.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/alaka-5-1536x1078.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /><figcaption class="wp-element-caption">Installation view of &#8216;Your Birth is My Birth.&#8217; Photo by Adam Reich</figcaption></figure>

		<item>
		<title>How Fatinha Ramos Channels ‘Visual Activism’ in Her Richly Layered Illustrations</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/fatinha-ramos-illustrations/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Grace Ebert]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 06 May 2026 16:02:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Art]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Illustration]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[activism]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[art history]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[disability]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[emotions]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Fatinha Ramos]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473449</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-4.jpeg" alt="How Fatinha Ramos Channels ‘Visual Activism’ in Her Richly Layered Illustrations" />"Art should broaden how we see the world—and that includes how we see bodies, too.”</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/fatinha-ramos-illustrations/">How Fatinha Ramos Channels ‘Visual Activism’ in Her Richly Layered Illustrations</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-4.jpeg" alt="How Fatinha Ramos Channels ‘Visual Activism’ in Her Richly Layered Illustrations" />


<p>&#8220;To me, being a visual activist means I only illustrate stories that resonate with me deeply, by giving voice to minorities or social situations that need to be addressed,&#8221; says <a href="https://fatinha.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Fatinha Ramos</a>. &#8220;It is the only way I can truly connect with others.&#8221;</p>



<p>Based in Antwerp, the Portuguese artist and illustrator is well-known for blending analog and digital techniques to create rich, emotive compositions. Collaborating with clients like <em>The New York Times</em>, <em>The Washington Post</em>, Tate, and <em>Scientific American</em>, among many others, Ramos has cultivated a keen eye for storytelling through her distinctive visual language.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2250" height="2000" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2.jpeg" alt="an illustration by Fatinha Ramos of herself and Frida Kahlo in bed with red-stemmed plants growing from their bodies" class="wp-image-473712" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2.jpeg 2250w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2-640x569.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2-960x853.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2-768x683.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2-1536x1365.jpeg 1536w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-2-2048x1820.jpeg 2048w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2250px) 100vw, 2250px" /></figure>



<p>Recent partnerships include the Anne Frank Museum and MoMA, the latter of which commissioned the artist to illustrate <a href="https://www.moma.org/magazine/articles/1374" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">an essay</a> on her experience being compared to <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/frida-kahlo/">Frida Kahlo</a>. Ramos was born with osteogenesis imperfecta, commonly called <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Osteogenesis_imperfecta" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">brittle bone disease</a>, which spurred a childhood spent in and out of hospitals. Drawing and art-making quickly became a preferred pastime, allowing her to transport herself from such clinical settings.</p>



<p>This adolescent hobby stuck, and Ramos worked as an art director in advertising and publishing for 12 years before venturing out on her own. Boasting an impressive list of clients and collaborators, she considers her practice to be an antidote to stereotypical narratives, whether related to the climate crisis, sexism, racism, or the dire lack of empathy that seems rampant in today&#8217;s world.</p>



<p>&#8220;I want to move away from the narrative that turns artists with disabilities into symbols of resilience,” she tells MoMA. “Creativity does not happen despite limitations but through them. Art should broaden how we see the world—and that includes how we see bodies, too.”</p>



<p>At the moment, Ramos is only accepting select illustration clients as she focuses on her fine art practice, including a series of anatomical glass sculptures based on brittle bone disease. You can explore more of her practice on <a href="https://fatinha.com/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">her website</a> and <a href="https://www.instagram.com/fatinharamos/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="1600" height="1928" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8.jpeg" alt="an illustration by Fatinha Ramos of a woman crying with leaves falling in the background" class="wp-image-473718" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8.jpeg 1600w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8-640x771.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8-960x1157.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8-768x925.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/ramos-8-1275x1536.jpeg 1275w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 1600px) 100vw, 1600px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>NASA Just Dropped More Than 12,000 Photos from the Artemis II Mission</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-earth-photography/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Wed, 06 May 2026 14:42:34 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Science]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[astronomy]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Earth]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[moon]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[NASA]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[space]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[stars]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473737</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-7.jpg" alt="NASA Just Dropped More Than 12,000 Photos from the Artemis II Mission" />Explore thousands of images taken by the Artemis II astronauts during their 10-day flyby mission around the moon.</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/nasa-artemis-ii-moon-earth-photography/">NASA Just Dropped More Than 12,000 Photos from the Artemis II Mission</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-7.jpg" alt="NASA Just Dropped More Than 12,000 Photos from the Artemis II Mission" />


<p>When it comes to photo dumps, <a href="/tags/nasa">NASA</a> has upped the ante. The organization has added thousands of snapshots from the Artemis II mission to the <a href="https://eol.jsc.nasa.gov/SearchPhotos/ShowQueryResults-Lightcycle.pl?results=177798551313402" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Gateway to Astronaut Photography of Earth</a> archive. The album now holds 12,217 images by cosmic travelers Reid Wiseman, Victor Glover, Christina Koch, and Jeremy Hansen during their more than 250,000-mile, <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/04/artemis-ii-earthset-moon-nasa-space-travel/">10-day flyby mission</a> around the moon.</p>



<p>According to <a href="https://petapixel.com/2026/05/04/nasa-releases-thousands-of-unseen-artemis-ii-photos/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">PetaPixel</a>, a couple of Nikons and an iPhone 17 were the cameras of choice for the journey. And even though many of the thousands of recently uploaded images are very similar—some are even quite blurry—scrolling through them gives the impression of being seated right next to the &#8220;<a href="https://www.nasa.gov/news-release/nasa-welcomes-record-setting-artemis-ii-moonfarers-back-to-earth/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Moonfarers</a>&#8221; as they marvel at Earth and its satellite and simply can&#8217;t put the camera down—just like we tend to snap way too many photos of a beautiful sunset.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1125" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10.jpg" alt="The Earth seen through a window in the Orion module during the Artemis II mission" class="wp-image-473740" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10-640x360.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10-960x540.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10-768x432.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-10-1536x864.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>Some of the most impactful photos include the reflections of the astronauts&#8217; hands and faces in the window of their vehicle, the Orion module. Juxtaposed with meticulously engineered equipment, the earth and moon seem somehow less abstracted from this unique vantage point, in which these orbs appear somehow more resonant and precious—and vulnerable.</p>



<p>Explore more of our favorites below, and learn about the Artemis II mission on <a href="https://www.nasa.gov/humans-in-space/artemis/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">NASA&#8217;s site</a>.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1125" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11.jpg" alt="A crescent-shaped view of the Earth, mostly obscured by shadow" class="wp-image-473741" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11-640x360.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11-960x540.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11-768x432.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-11-1536x864.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1125" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9.jpg" alt="The Moon seen through a window in the Orion module during the Artemis II mission" class="wp-image-473748" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9-640x360.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9-960x540.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9-768x432.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-9-1536x864.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1125" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8.jpg" alt="A total eclipse seen from the Orion module of the Artemis II mission" class="wp-image-473747" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8-640x360.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8-960x540.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8-768x432.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-8-1536x864.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1334" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5.jpeg" alt="Stars seen through a window in the Orion module during the Artemis II mission" class="wp-image-473744" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5.jpeg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5-640x427.jpeg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5-960x640.jpeg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5-768x512.jpeg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/artemisii-5-1536x1025.jpeg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>

		<item>
		<title>Janusz Jurek Embraces the Weirdness of Everyday Life in Captivating Street Photographs</title>
		<link>https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/janusz-jurek-street-photography/</link>
		
		<dc:creator><![CDATA[Kate Mothes]]></dc:creator>
		<pubDate>Tue, 05 May 2026 18:30:00 +0000</pubDate>
				<category><![CDATA[Photography]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[humor]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[Janusz Jurek]]></category>
		<category><![CDATA[street photography]]></category>
		<guid isPermaLink="false">https://www.thisiscolossal.com/?p=473693</guid>

					<description><![CDATA[<p><img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-8.jpg" alt="Janusz Jurek Embraces the Weirdness of Everyday Life in Captivating Street Photographs" />"For me, street photography is the antithesis of all the technical perfection and imperfection that's everywhere on the internet these days."</p>
<p>Do stories and artists like this matter to you? Become a <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/members">Colossal Member</a> today and support independent arts publishing for as little as $7 per month. The article <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/2026/05/janusz-jurek-street-photography/">Janusz Jurek Embraces the Weirdness of Everyday Life in Captivating Street Photographs</a> appeared first on <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com">Colossal</a>.</p>
]]></description>
										<content:encoded><![CDATA[<img src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-8.jpg" alt="Janusz Jurek Embraces the Weirdness of Everyday Life in Captivating Street Photographs" />


<p>Humor and happenstance take the front seat in Polish photographer <a href="https://januszjurek.info/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Janusz Jurek</a>’s wry images. Working as a graphic designer and commercial photographer by day, he finds the greatest creative freedom in the candid and incidental—the things he notices as he moves about town, travels, and attends festivals and other events. These are the places where he observes some of the most unique individuals and the quirkiest coincidences. &#8220;The less commercial and more bizarre, the better—people are more authentic then, less in control of what they&#8217;re doing,&#8221; he tells Colossal.</p>



<p>Jurek is drawn to situations that happen outside of the mainstream, often turning his back on whatever the present attraction is in order to observe what&#8217;s happening all around him. He focuses on &#8220;the people, their reactions, small gestures, and strange coincidences. This is where moments that are truly surprising often appear,&#8221; he says.</p>



<figure class="wp-block-image size-full"><img loading="lazy" decoding="async" width="2000" height="1333" src="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3.jpg" alt="A candid street photograph by Janusz Jurek of textiles hanging on a drying line and someone's legs sticking out from behind one of the pieces" class="wp-image-473699" srcset="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3.jpg 2000w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3-640x427.jpg 640w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3-960x640.jpg 960w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3-768x512.jpg 768w, https://www.thisiscolossal.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/05/jurek-3-1536x1024.jpg 1536w" sizes="auto, (max-width: 2000px) 100vw, 2000px" /></figure>



<p>As Jurek has learned over time, some of the best images happen right at home. The crux of the process is all about noticing what&#8217;s going on, not where it happens. And beauty is never the objective. &#8220;I don&#8217;t care about the photos being pretty,&#8221; he says. &#8220;Quite the opposite—for me, street photography is the antithesis of all the technical perfection and imperfection that&#8217;s everywhere on the internet these days.&#8221; Instead, he&#8217;s fascinated by the ability to raise questions and provoke reactions in the viewer, from curiosity to amusement to slight discomfort.</p>



<p>Jurek is working toward the release of a collection of photos titled <em>Look, Before It&#8217;s Gone</em>, chronicling his street photography over a period of five years. See more on <a href="https://www.behance.net/januszjurek" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Behance</a>, and follow updates on <a href="https://www.instagram.com/januszjurek.info/" target="_blank" rel="noreferrer noopener">Instagram</a>. You might also enjoy the work of <a href="/tags/eric-kogan">Eric Kogan</a> and perusing top images in the <a href="https://www.thisiscolossal.com/tags/pure-street-photography/">Pure Street Photography Awards</a>.</p>
